condition: Right-sided colon ischaemia — acute mesenteric ischaemia to be excluded
permutationLabel: Isolated right colon ischaemia, AF off anticoagulation, lactate 4.1
summary: 79-year-old man with AF (anticoagulation stopped after a fall) and severe periumbilical pain out of proportion, then maroon stools; lactate 4.1; CT shows right colonic wall thickening. ACG 2015: isolated right colon ischaemia → CT angiography to exclude acute mesenteric ischaemia (SMA embolus).

inputs.chiefComplaint: Severe tummy pain with dark blood from the back passage
inputs.hpi: Six hours of severe central abdominal pain, came on over minutes, much worse than it looks on examination; vomited twice, then two maroon stools. Atrial fibrillation; apixaban stopped 2 months ago after a fall. Previous myocardial infarction.

exam.general: Distressed. HR 112 irregularly irregular, BP 104/66, T 37.2°C, RR 22.
exam.abdomen: Soft, mild right-sided tenderness only; pain out of proportion to the findings. No peritonism.

imaging.name: CT abdomen/pelvis (portal venous phase)
imaging.result: Wall thickening of the caecum and ascending colon with surrounding stranding; SMA not assessed (no arterial phase). No free gas.

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Isolated right colon ischaemia — acute mesenteric ischaemia not excluded
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Isolated right colon ischaemia in AF off anticoagulation with lactate 4.1 and pain out of proportion: acute mesenteric ischaemia (SMA embolus) must be excluded with CT angiography; vascular surgery.

mustNotMiss.knownGapNote: Acute mesenteric ischaemia is not a PANE disease (top 3: appendicitis, hernia, cholecystitis); symptom inference ranks it #1. Same gap as the appendicitis seed vignettes.
mustNotMiss.proposedFix: Add acute mesenteric ischaemia to PANE (AF/embolic source, pain out of proportion, lactate) and a CTA-first protocol (ESVS 2017).

mustInclude.note: ACG 2015: isolated right colon ischaemia warrants CT angiography to exclude occlusive SMA disease; ESVS 2017: CTA for suspected AMI.
mustInclude.knownGapNote: K55.0 maps to the ischaemic_colitis protocol, whose imaging is "CT abdomen/pelvis with IV contrast"; nothing asks for CT angiography when the ischaemia is right-sided or embolic.
mustInclude.proposedFix: In the ischaemic colitis protocol add: isolated right colon ischaemia, AF or lactate rise → CT angiography to exclude AMI (ACG 2015).

mustInclude.knownGapNote: Web, since the engine-matching fixes (2026-09): this passed only on the "Emergency laparotomy consent" line of the peritonism prompt, which fired on negated peritonism. No vascular/revascularisation output exists for right-sided ischaemia with AMI not excluded.

guideline.name: ACG clinical guideline — colon ischaemia
guideline.section: Isolated right colon ischaemia: evaluate the mesenteric vasculature (CTA) — higher mortality and association with AMI
guideline.citation: Brandt LJ, Feuerstadt P, Longstreth GF, Boley SJ. ACG clinical guideline: epidemiology, risk factors, patterns of presentation, diagnosis, and management of colon ischemia (CI). Am J Gastroenterol. 2015;110:18–44.

guideline.name: ESVS clinical practice guidelines — diseases of the mesenteric arteries and veins
guideline.section: Suspected acute mesenteric ischaemia: CT angiography without delay; revascularisation
guideline.citation: Björck M, Koelemay M, Acosta S, et al. Management of the diseases of mesenteric arteries and veins: clinical practice guidelines of the European Society of Vascular Surgery (ESVS). Eur J Vasc Endovasc Surg. 2017;53:460–510.

rationale: Permutation: the right-sided/embolic variant. The portal-venous CT already done does not exclude an SMA embolus; the plan must ask for CTA.
